THE_COUNTER_IS_WRONG_AND_HERE_IS_WHY: Recorded 2026-08-30. This file says one run. Three page gate runs were actually performed and paid for: run 1 at 14:23 (98 claims, $10.89), run 2 with --since ($7.55), and a new-cycle run ($13.37). Only the first wrote anything here, because factcheck_draft.py records a run ONLY when --report is given — 'if not args.report: return', and the cycle_record call sits behind the same condition. The commands for runs 2 and 3 were written by claude and omitted --report. So $20.92 of gating produced no artifact, no sha binding, and no increment to the cap that exists to stop exactly that kind of spending. The ADJUDICATIONS from those runs stand: they were made from the runs' real terminal output, which the operator pasted, and every change they produced is in the page and in draft_decisions.json. What is missing is the machine-readable evidence and the counter. Two files were also committed under names claiming to preserve run 2 and the new-cycle run. Both were byte-identical copies of the run 1 report. They have been moved to _to_delete/false-gate-reports/ rather than left in the repository under names that describe evidence that does not exist.
CAN_THE_LOST_REPORTS_BE_RECONSTRUCTED: Asked by the operator, 2026-08-30. NO, and the money is the smaller reason. (1) The terminal output carries only the claims that FAILED — 29 of 100 on the new-cycle run — plus 2 of 19 recency entries. It carries no claim ids, no claim objects, no sha256, and nothing at all about the 71 claims that passed. A file built from it would be a different document wearing the report's name. (2) Writing that file by hand into the path publish.py reads as the gate's own verdict would be manufacturing evidence, which is a worse fault than the one it would paper over. (3) DECISIVE: the page has changed about ten times since the last run, including three edits that fix errors that run found. A report bound to the pre-fix sha cannot certify the post-fix text. A confirming run was owed regardless, so the lost artifacts change what we have, not what we must do next. What the spending bought was the FINDINGS, and the findings survive: they were adjudicated from the runs' real output and every fix is in the page, the email and draft_decisions.json. What it failed to buy was the certificate, and a certificate for a superseded draft would have been worthless anyway.
THE_FIX: --report now defaults to <draft>.gate.json in factcheck_draft.py. The trap was that its absence silently disabled both save() and cycle_record(), so a run printed its findings, wrote nothing, and left the cap counter untouched.
